title: Data Splitting & Overfitting 🧪
description: Learn about train/validation/test splits and recognize overfitting.

slides.title: The Golden Rule of ML 🏅
slides.content:
# Never Test on Training Data!

We split data into:
* **Training set**: used to update weights.
* **Validation set**: used to tune hyperparameters and monitor overfitting.
* **Test set**: used only once at the end to report final performance.

Typical split: 70% train, 15% val, 15% test.

slides.title: Manual Data Split
slides.content: Using simple slicing on a tensor dataset.
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch

X = torch.randn(100, 4)
y = torch.randint(0, 3, (100,))

n = len(X)
train_n = int(0.7 * n)
val_n = int(0.15 * n)

X_train, y_train = X[:train_n], y[:train_n]
X_val, y_val = X[train_n:train_n+val_n], y[train_n:train_n+val_n]
X_test, y_test = X[train_n+val_n:], y[train_n+val_n:]
print(len(X_train), len(X_val), len(X_test))

quizData.question: Why do we need a validation set?

options.text: To tune hyperparameters and detect overfitting

quizData.explanation: Validation set provides unbiased evaluation during hyperparameter tuning.

slides.title: What is Overfitting? 🎯🎪
slides.content:
## When Memorization Hurts

Overfitting: the model performs great on training data but poorly on unseen data. Signs:
* Training loss continues to decrease.
* Validation loss starts to increase.

Opposite: Underfitting – model fails to learn patterns even on training data.

slides.title: Simulating Overfitting (Conceptual)
slides.content: Training loss vs validation loss divergence.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Example of tracking losses (conceptual)
train_losses = [0.8, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1]
val_losses = [0.9, 0.7, 0.6, 0.7, 0.85, 1.0]
# Early: both improve; later: val loss rises = overfitting

quizData.question: Which scenario indicates overfitting?

options.text: Both training and validation loss decreasing
Training loss decreasing, validation loss increasing
Validation loss lower than training loss

quizData.explanation: Overfitting: model fits training noise; generalization worsens.

slides.title: Regularization Tools 🛡️
slides.content:
## Fight Overfitting

* **Dropout**: randomly zeroes neurons during training.
* **Weight decay** (L2 regularization): penalizes large weights.
* **Early stopping**: halt when val loss stops improving.
* **More data** / **data augmentation**: best cure!

We'll see these in action.

slides.title: Dropout Example
slides.codeSnippet:
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(10, 20),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Dropout(0.5),  # 50% dropout during training
    nn.Linear(20, 1)
)
print(model)
